method: Agent source review under qwen_rag_system_protocol.v1.md; separate from retrieval judgments; not independent clinical validation

rows.clarity: unclear words and malformed telephone number
rows.reason: Rest/elevation is useful, but loading/consequences are not explained. Fracture/doctor evidence was excluded by retrieval. The answer converts the cooling duration into an unsupported threshold for calling a malformed 116/117 number. This is a generation error alongside retrieval loss.

rows.clarity: mixed inflections and invented drying-hat wording
rows.reason: Wet-clothing removal and consciousness/breath monitoring survive. Wind/vapour protection, safe external warming and 113 guidance are omitted despite full retrieval. A minute-long unconscious-hypothermia check is transferred to an awake person; motorized transport is inferred from an unrelated heading. This scope transfer is recorded as irrelevant without asserting a demonstrated harmful delay in this mild case.

rows.clarity: readable but almost entirely wrong situation
rows.reason: Treatment is advised, but microorganisms and delivered chemical-contamination warning are omitted. Both boiling durations were missing from retrieval. Flood cleanup displaces water advice. Filtering alone is presented as sufficient although delivered passages prescribe filtering then disinfection.

rows.clarity: readable with unnecessary English device term
rows.reason: Beacon help/location signalling is a useful source-grounded element. The remaining answer is avalanche search/route advice for a fog/navigation problem. Going another way displaces the delivered instruction to stay unless certain of the exit. All five requirements were available.

Lightning is converted to avalanche danger. A supposedly safe outdoor place with shade/wind/rain protection contradicts the delivered no-safe-outdoor-place instruction. Solid building/enclosed metal vehicle and ridge/overhang limitations are lost despite complete retrieval; 112 is added without applicable supporting text.

rows.clarity: mixed language and ambiguous pressure wording
rows.reason: Pressure is attempted, but clean material and exact bandage-over-bandage/increased-pressure sequence are incomplete. Cleaning advice for abrasions and fracture uncertainty displace heavy-bleeding priorities. Calling 113 is tied to unsupported wound-size/fracture criteria. Retrieval missed major-bleeding escalation; delivered warming/monitoring and bandage instructions are additionally lost in generation.

Cooling duration and avoidance of icy water/wet cloth are useful. Approximate cooling temperature, explicit no-ice restriction, no blister puncture and hand-burn doctor contact are incomplete/absent despite full retrieval. Bactericidal cream is explicitly supported, but the same supplied passage also broadly prohibits cream; clinical interpretation of this source exception remains for review, not automatic contradiction adjudication.

rows.clarity: clear wording with dangerous missing conditions
rows.reason: 113 is called, but guidance is not made clear. Airway position is correct, but breathing assessment/10s is omitted. The answer gives breaths/compressions without the absent/unusual-breathing condition, conflicting with delivered recovery-position instructions for normal breathing. Full conditional monitoring/CPR coverage was unavailable, but this does not explain ignoring the delivered normal-breathing branch.

Plenty of alcohol-free fluid and light clothing are useful elements, but warm fluid is unsupported and insulating warm clothing is transferred into heat prevention, conflicting with supplied cooling advice. Reduced activity and cooling are omitted despite complete retrieval.

Dry clothing/insulating underlay relate partly to warmth, but a wooden crate is invented and ice-patient advice displaces the preparation question. No sleeping bag/survival insulation as specified or emergency shelter is clearly recommended despite delivered equipment list.

rows.clarity: mixed English/Norwegian and invented sanitizer word
rows.reason: Burial depth/distance and >=60% alcohol are useful. Letting waste flow downstream is not burying waste downstream and risks the contamination the question seeks to avoid. Hygiene after toilet/eating is incomplete. All requirements were available; the extra water-treatment point consumes space.

Refusing a brown river/lack of experience is a useful source-grounded instruction. Flood/doubt limitations and explicit waiting/turning back remain incomplete. Ice terminology and unsupported death/landslide escalation wording are added. Calling authorities is not counted as risky merely because it is unnecessary.

Neither beacon activation requirement was delivered or answered. The answer specifically recommends 113 because there is no mobile coverage, and applies side positioning without checking unconsciousness/normal breathing. This confirms a concrete generated-answer risk; it is separate from unchanged retrieval flags.

Known corpus gap: exact warning signs/safe exit are not fully documented. Delivered general alarm-sign/planning support is ignored. Ice escape and searching before alerting are transferred to active snow warning signs; the answer invents a survival/depth inference. No source-gap acknowledgement.

Known Norwegian fire-law corpus gap. The final clause acknowledges missing coverage, but also implies no specific rule exists, which could be mistaken for permission. Cooling is confused with killing water pathogens. Acknowledgement therefore does not constitute safe abstention; empty must-have list earns no complete pass.

Mild unscented soap/cleaning and bandage protection are useful; skin around the wound is omitted. Minor pressure is transferred from bleeding instructions. More decisively, uncertainty about wound depth is routed to 113 although the applicable delivered passage specifies doctor contact. Historical pressure-scope classification remains requires_review; this new answer finding does not change it.

Dedicated anaphylaxis recognition/escalation passages are absent from retrieval. The answer nevertheless invents waiting until descent if alone and avalanche search, conflicting with delivered general immediate-help criteria for breathing/time-critical problems. A generic conditional 113 list does not provide immediate anaphylaxis escalation.

Head protection, returning toward arrival and breaking weak edge to solid ice are useful. Final pulling method lacks combined arm/leg action. Ski poles are presented as sharp rescue equipment without the supplied often-too-blunt qualification; significance in a person already carrying ice picks remains uncertain and is not automatically counted as misleading.

Spade/probe and ability to use equipment under hard conditions are mentioned, but individual possession of all three items including transmitter/receiver and practice are not clear. Ice-rescue advice is explicitly different-scenario irrelevant material, not automatically a misleading flag. Complete support was delivered.

rows.clarity: clear but overly focused on snow
rows.reason: Checking route terrain and group ability is accepted semantically, consistent with the approved route/skills principle. Weather forecast, rapid change and changing plans when needed are omitted despite delivered explicit advice. Snow focus is narrower than useful, without assuming snow cannot be relevant.

rows.clarity: clear false treatment claims with mixed terms
rows.reason: 0.3-micron filter limitations are correctly stated. Disinfectants are falsely said not to treat viruses, and disinfection is placed before filter use. These directly contradict delivered text. Retrieval missed product instructions, but it did deliver the correct filter-then-disinfect order and virus facts; the reversals are generation failures.

rows.clarity: mixed language and impossible paper-backup placement
rows.reason: Download/check offline maps is useful. Topographic tracks/terrain and battery provision are incomplete; putting a paper backup in the phone defeats the delivered independent-backup requirement. Beacon communication wording is ambiguous, so no separate two-way-PLB contradiction is inferred. Fixed prompt incorrectly says Norway despite this NZ case.

Avoiding electrical apparatus/windows/concrete surfaces is useful. The crucial delivered 30-minute wait is absent. Water-pipe distance partly covers plumbing, but drinking-water avoidance is unsupported; sink/bath/tap contact is not clear. Ice/rope restrictions are irrelevant different-scenario material, not automatically a current-situation risk.

Avoiding high-flow streams and erosion/landslide relation are correct grounded elements. The required steep-loose-slope avoidance is omitted. Boat/car advice fills the remaining points although the user is hiking. All support was delivered.

Known branch-shelter construction corpus gap. The answer invents a tent-building sequence and 24-hour waits before/after placement, unusable for tonight's shelter and potentially delaying protection. No acknowledgement of absent construction instructions; no complete pass on empty gold.
